text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak holds two summit meetings with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad and King Hussein of Jordan. The talks dealt with ways to face obstacles on the road towards peace. In a press conference, Mubarak said the substitute to peace would be dangerous for all countries in and outside the region, including Israel.
- Mubarak tells chief editors of Egyptian newspapers that he has sent a message to U.S. President Bill Clinton on the seriousness of continuing Jewish settlements.
- Mubarak tells the television programme 'City Talk' that Egypt's stand concerning the Doha economic conference has not been decided yet. The U.S. aid is not a means of pressure on Egypt, he says.
- The Cabinet will discuss today a number of economic reports on encouraging investment.
- Security authorities arrested a terrorist, responsible for financing the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) in the southern province of Assiut.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi approved a number of plans, which aim at fighting negative phenomena on the Egyptian street, such as pegging, thuggery and homeless juveniles.
